capture_lineage: Captured by the operator's assistant via approved, human-triggered public web research restricted to the official Amazon Ads domain. The toolkit itself performed no Amazon fetch: core/amazon_docs_contract.py ships an empty VERIFIED_OFFICIAL_PREFIXES allowlist, so every concrete Amazon URL is denied AMAZON_PUBLIC_DOCUMENTATION_UNVERIFIED. This snapshot is advisory input to a human-reviewed decision, never an executable rule or a product fact.
account_scope_note: Rules can differ by locale, account age, seller-vs-vendor/author registration, and owner-configurable settings. Every value below must be re-confirmed by the owner from the live US Amazon Ads console before any Release 7.1M/7.2 use. Do not silently choose the most aggressive interpretation.

topics.page_title: Best practices for your Sponsored Products ads | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: To advertise with Sponsored Products a product must be in one or more eligible categories and be eligible for the Featured Offer. Adult products, used products, refurbished products, and products in closed categories are not supported.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: Category eligibility varies by marketplace and can change; confirm the specific product's category eligibility in the live US console.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms the advertised ASIN is in an eligible, non-closed category from the live US Ads console.

topics.page_title: Best practices for your Sponsored Products ads | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: A product must be in stock and priced competitively to win the Featured Offer. If the offer is not the Featured Offer or is out of stock, the Sponsored Products ad will not display.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: For FBM, in-stock means the owner's production/handling capacity can fulfill; there is no Amazon-managed inventory count. Owner must confirm real fulfillment capacity.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms live buyable in-stock status and FBM handling capacity.

topics.topic: Featured Offer requirement and SKU-level implication
topics.page_title: Best practices for your Sponsored Products ads | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Featured Offer eligibility is required to advertise a product with Sponsored Products. The Featured Offer is determined at the offer (SKU) level; the specific advertised SKU must itself be Featured-Offer eligible and competitively priced.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: Featured Offer state is dynamic and SKU/offer-specific; for a single-seller private listing it typically resolves to the seller's own offer, but this must be confirmed live.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms the advertised SKU currently holds/qualifies for the Featured Offer in the live US console.

topics.page_title: A guide to targeting with Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Advertisers can let Amazon target relevant keywords/products automatically (automatic targeting) or choose keywords and product targets themselves (manual targeting). Amazon recommends starting with automatic targeting.
topics.revalidation_requirement: None beyond confirming current console options.

topics.topic: Broad, phrase, and exact match types
topics.page_title: Understand keyword match types | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Keyword targeting supports three match types: broad (widest reach; query may contain the terms in any order and may include plurals, variations, synonyms, related terms), phrase (more restrictive than broad), and exact (most restrictive; typically highest conversion rate).
topics.revalidation_requirement: None beyond confirming current console behavior.

topics.page_title: A guide to targeting with Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Negative keywords (available as negative exact and negative phrase) prevent ads from showing on shopping queries that do not meet campaign objectives. They are a control to exclude traffic, never an automatic allocation of unallocated keywords.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: Negative product targeting also exists (ASIN/brand) but is distinct from negative keywords.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner decides negatives explicitly; the toolkit never auto-converts unallocated eligible keywords into negatives.

topics.page_title: A guide to targeting with Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: A Sponsored Products campaign's targeting type (automatic vs manual) is chosen at creation; automatic and manual targeting are generally run as separate campaigns rather than switched within one campaign.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: The public guide did not restate this rule verbatim during capture; it reflects long-standing console behavior. Treat as owner-confirmable, not authoritative from this snapshot.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms current console rule for changing/segregating targeting types before any campaign structuring in 7.1M.

topics.topic: Dynamic down-only, dynamic up-and-down, fixed, and rule-based bidding availability
topics.page_title: Guide to dynamic bidding - up and down with Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Sponsored Products offers fixed bids (uses the entered bid), dynamic bids - down only (Amazon lowers the bid when a click seems less likely to convert), and dynamic bids - up and down (Amazon raises up to 100% for placements more likely to convert and lowers otherwise). Rule-based bidding (ROAS guardrails) and schedule-based bid rules are also available in campaign manager.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: The up to 100% figure is the dynamic bid-adjustment ceiling for placements, NOT a budget/daily-spend multiplier. Do not conflate the two.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms which strategies are currently available on the account.

topics.topic: Daily budget monthly averaging and intraday pacing
topics.page_title: Budgets-the basics and best practices for Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: The daily budget is averaged over a calendar month: on a given day actual spend can be less than, or up to 25% more than, the average daily budget, while monthly spend averages out to the daily budget times the number of days.
topics.verbatim_quote: Your daily budget is averaged over the course of a calendar month. That means you could spend less than or up to 25% more than your average daily budget on any given day.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: The 25% intraday overage and monthly-averaging behavior has changed historically and can vary; it must not be hardcoded. This is the exact value the Phase 7 spec forbids baking in.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms current daily-budget overage behavior from the live US console; 7.1M must read it, not assume 25% (and never 200%).

topics.page_title: A complete guide to budget rules | Amazon Ads
topics.paraphrased_rule: Budget rules in campaign manager let advertisers automatically adjust budgets during a time frame or against a performance target. The platform's own daily overage behavior (currently up to 25% intraday, monthly-averaged) is not described as an advertiser-configurable percentage.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: Budget rules (advertiser-set) are distinct from the platform's intraday overage mechanic. Do not model a universal exposure multiplier from either.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms budget-rule availability and any account-level overage/pacing settings live.

topics.page_title: Attribution methodology | Amazon Ads Support Center
topics.paraphrased_rule: Attribution lookback windows differ by program and registration. Amazon Attribution uses a 14-day last-touch window. Sponsored Products conversion attribution differs for sellers versus vendors/authors and must not be assumed identical across account types.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: The seller-vs-vendor/author distinction is real and must be preserved; the exact SP seller window (commonly cited as 7 days for sellers) was not locked to a verbatim official quote during capture. Confirm live.
topics.revalidation_requirement: Owner confirms the account type (seller) and the exact SP attribution window from the live US console/reports before any realized-PPC math in 7.2.

topics.topic: Manually downloadable reports relevant to future Release 7.2
topics.page_title: Search term report for Sponsored Products | Amazon Ads Support Center
topics.paraphrased_rule: Sponsored Products reporting is available as downloadable reports and within the console (e.g., search term report, campaign/targeting/placement reports). These are owner-exported files; automated retrieval from the account is prohibited by the toolkit's permanent Amazon boundary.
topics.conflicting_or_locale_specific: Report availability/columns evolve; the owner exports manually. The toolkit never pulls account reports.
topics.revalidation_requirement: For 7.2 the owner manually exports reports; the toolkit ingests owner-provided files only.
